question: Is the proposed retrieval-agnostic semantic+temporal relevance framework already covered by existing work (e.g., a hybrid lexical+dense+exponential-temporal-decay framework with a temporal benchmark, or an as-of temporal RAG), leaving little novelty?
description: Two retrieved items appear to occupy the proposed space: a 'Bridging the Temporal-Semantic Gap' paper that proposes a three-signal hybrid framework (BM25 + dense + exponential temporal decay) and a trilingual temporal benchmark, and a 'Temporal-Logical Decay Architecture' (Chronofy) for time-aware RAG. If confirmed by full-text reading, the idea's mechanism and benchmark contribution are largely pre-empted; the remaining delta would be domain (statutes/regulations) and the retrieval-agnostic framing.
confidence_basis: Concrete mechanism-level comparisons across the three closest systems plus a legal benchmark, each supported by verified quotes, and the earlier finding that the closest legal framework reports no empirical comparison. Residual uncertainty is only about whether very recent unpublished work repeats the measurement design.
rationale: Titles and the available abstract of the 'Bridging the Temporal-Semantic Gap' paper explicitly describe combining lexical, dense, and exponential temporal decay signals and building a temporal benchmark -- the core of the proposed method.
resolution: Resolved: each component of the original framework is already published in some form. Semantic plus temporal hybrid ranking is the three-signal BM25+dense+exponential-decay framework on a temporal benchmark; learnable temporal decay plus explicit temporal-validity evaluation is Chronofy, which embeds validity into representation, retrieval and reasoning; hard as-of gating with a temporal-evidence-leakage metric is TempFinRAG for point-in-time financial QA; and temporal validity in legal evaluation is already encoded in a legal reasoning benchmark. Remaining differences are packaging (post-hoc layer vs modified representation/retrieval layers; hard valid-time gate vs learnable decay) and measurement (clause-version identity labels rather than MCQA; retrieval-time enforcement tested across base retrievers). Treating the temporal relevance term itself as the contribution is therefore an implementation-level difference, not novelty.
